text:
The suspect should be found **not guilty** of assault. On his account, the arrest was complete when the officer began striking him, so the punch was self-defense against excessive force, not force used "in resisting arrest" under the statute. The shared note's test (guilty if the arrest was unlawful) doesn't fit this statute, which turns on whether the suspect knew he was being arrested, not on whether the arrest was lawful. If the jury accepts the officer's account, the punch came during resistance and the suspect would be guilty, so the outcome turns on which account is believed.

CONFIDENCE: 55
